results.content: Mauna Loa, the world’s largest active volcano, located on the south-central part of the island of Hawaii, Hawaii state, U.S., and a part of Hawaii Volcanoes National Park. It is an active volcano, with its last eruption in 2022. Mauna Loa is significant not only for its size but also for its ongoing impact on human activity in Hawaii, where communities continue to develop and persist in volcanic risk zones while relying on monitoring and emergency preparedness to manage potential hazards. [...] Hawaii Volcanoes National Park, established in 1961, is an active volcanic area located along the southeastern shore of Hawaii island in the United States. Encompassing 505 square miles (1,308 square km), the park includes two active volcanoes, Mauna Loa and Kilauea, which are 25 miles (40 km) apart. Mauna Loa is the world’s largest volcano, and Kilauea is considered to be the world’s most active volcano. The park, which was designated a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1987, also features unusual [...] Mauna Loa, located in the south-central part of the island, is Earth’s largest volcano. Its bulk extends upward about 3 miles (5 km) from the ocean bottom, then rises an additional 2.6 miles (4.2 km) to an elevation of 13,677 feet (4,169 metres) above sea level. Covering half of the island, Mauna Loa is a shield volcano that has erupted some three dozen times since its first well-documented eruption in 1843. The eruption began in Mokuʻāweoweo, the summit caldera of Mauna Loa, around 11:30 p.m. HST on Sunday November 27, 2022. After several hours, new fissures opened some distance away from the summit along the Northeast Rift Zone. Soonafter, the summit fissures stopped erupting.
